verses.text: David asked, "Is anyone still left from Saul's family? I want to show him kindness for Jonathan's sake."
There was a servant from Saul's family named Ziba, and they called him to come to David. The king asked him, "Are you Ziba?" He answered, "I am your servant."
The king asked, "Is there anyone still alive from Saul's family? I want to show him God's kindness." Ziba answered the king, "Jonathan still has a son who is crippled in both feet."
The king asked, "Where is he?" Ziba said, "He is at the house of Makir son of Ammiel, in Lo Debar."
So King David sent for him and had him brought from the house of Makir son of Ammiel in Lo Debar.
Mephibosheth, the son of Jonathan and grandson of Saul, came to David and bowed down low with his face to the ground. David said, "Mephibosheth?" He answered, "I am your servant."

David said to him, "Don't be afraid. I will certainly be kind to you for the sake of your father Jonathan. I will give back to you all the land that belonged to your grandfather Saul, and you will always eat at my table."
Mephibosheth bowed down and said, "Who am I, your servant, that you should care about a dead dog like me?"
Then the king called Saul's servant Ziba and said to him, "I have given your master's grandson everything that belonged to Saul and his family.

You, your sons, and your servants must farm the land for him and bring in the harvest, so that your master's grandson will have food to eat. But Mephibosheth himself will always eat at my table." Ziba had fifteen sons and twenty servants.
Ziba said to the king, "I, your servant, will do everything my lord the king commands." So Mephibosheth ate at David's table like one of the king's own sons.
Mephibosheth had a young son named Mica. Everyone who lived in Ziba's house became Mephibosheth's servants.
So Mephibosheth lived in Jerusalem, because he always ate at the king's table. He was crippled in both feet.
